chunks: And Pharaoh said, "Bring to me every skilled magician."

key_terms.سَاحِرٍ: Magician, one who performs sorcery or illusion
key_terms.فِرْعَوْنُ: Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt in the time of Moses

ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh order his court to do regarding the magicians?
ai.summary: In the Shia exegetical tradition, this verse highlights Pharaoh's reliance on 'ilm' (knowledge) and 'sihr' (magic) as a form of arrogant epistemology to rival divine truth, a theme echoed in the concept of 'zulm' (oppression) where power is used to suppress prophecy. The gathering of 'every' skilled magician underscores the totality of Egypt's intellectual and mystical resources being mobilized against Moses (AS), setting the stage for the ultimate defeat of human artifice by divine sign. This event serves as a paradigm for the struggle between the elite's fabricated authority and the prophetic reality.
